title: Reusability report: multi-sample omics network inference operates in distinct robustness regimes defined by prior knowledge and data availability - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: A reusability report reproduces and extends CORNETO, a mixed-integer framework for multi-sample, prior-knowledge-constrained biological network inference. It finds the main benefit of joint inference is robustness rather than better prediction, with results depending on prior-network completeness and sample heterogeneity, and adds bootstrap aggregation and selective re-expansion to improve stability.

insights.claim: The principal benefit of multi-sample constrained inference across iMAT, KPNN, Steiner tree and CARNIVAL is improved robustness and reproducibility rather than uniformly better predictive performance.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Users should adopt joint inference for stability, not expect accuracy gains by default.
insights.quote: the principal benefit of multi-sample inference was improved robustness rather than uniformly improved predictive performance

insights.claim: The authors frame network reconstruction as a regime-dependent learning problem, in which the value of joint inference depends on the interplay among prior knowledge, biological heterogeneity, regularization and data availability.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Method choice should be diagnosed by data regime rather than applied uniformly.
insights.quote: position network reconstruction as a regime-dependent learning problem

insights.claim: Inferring regulatory networks from high-dimensional data is fundamentally underdetermined because several candidate structures can fit the same measurements, so predictive performance alone cannot show an inferred network matches the true molecular mechanism.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Benchmarks on fit alone overstate biological validity; identifiability and stability are the right tests.
insights.quote: predictive performance alone cannot establish that an inferred network corresponds to the underlying molecular regulatory mechanism

insights.claim: Multi-sample sFBA consistently produced smaller, more compact networks than single-condition FBA, with reduction of about 32% at 10% of optimal biomass versus about 6% at 90%, while run-to-run coefficient of variation rose from 2.9% to 8.9%.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Near-optimal growth constraints leave less room to prune and increase solution degeneracy.
insights.quote: At 10% of the optimal biomass, the networks were reduced by ~32%, whereas at 90%, the reduction decreased to ~6%
insights.locator: Evaluating the reproducibility of the reported results

insights.claim: KPNN ROC-AUC was highly stable across repeated runs on the T-cell-receptor stimulation dataset, with per-run deviation under 0.001, showing training stochasticity has minimal effect under fixed data splits.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Neural network-based network inference can be reproducible when splits are fixed.
insights.quote: the scores for the area under the curve of the receiver operating characteristic (ROC-AUC)36 remained highly stable across repeated runs
insights.locator: Evaluating the reproducibility of the reported results

insights.claim: In the haematopoiesis dataset, multi-sample Steiner tree inference achieved lower fitting error for the same edge fraction than single-sample runs and yielded up to 2-3 times higher edge recovery without increased error, with single-sample performance degrading sharply as terminals increased.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Joint inference helps most when problems are complex and noisy.
insights.quote: Joint inference across haematopoiesis replicates yielded up to ×2–3 higher edge recovery without increased error
insights.locator: Assessing CORNETO across dynamic and stable biological systems

insights.claim: With CARNIVAL at lambda 0.1 on haematopoietic data, the multi-sample model retained about 720 shared edges versus about 470-500 in single-sample runs at similar fitting error, and its performance declined more gradually as regularization increased.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Information sharing preserves signalling structure under stronger regularization.
insights.quote: the multi-sample model retained ~720 shared edges, compared with ~470–500 in single-sample runs
insights.locator: Assessing CORNETO across dynamic and stable biological systems

insights.claim: On the stable adult cortex dataset, gains from multi-sample coupling were less pronounced, CARNIVAL returned no feasible solutions probably due to extreme intercell-type homogeneity and class imbalance, and iMAT precision and recall stayed low.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Joint inference methods can fail outright in highly homogeneous data, so regime checks are needed first.
insights.quote: CARNIVAL did not return feasible solutions
insights.locator: Assessing CORNETO across dynamic and stable biological systems

insights.claim: The authors caution that each regime is represented by one dataset, so differences between dynamic and homeostatic systems are hypotheses, and with no experimental ground truth the results are supportive and hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of causal regulation.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Generalisation claims about dynamic versus stable systems are explicitly not established.
insights.quote: these observations should not be interpreted as establishing general differences between dynamic and homeostatic biological systems
insights.locator: Assessing CORNETO across dynamic and stable biological systems

insights.claim: Multi-sample CARNIVAL and Steiner tree recovered subnetworks that mirror developmental proximity, with MEP versus ERP the most coherent and MEP versus MPP, HSC and all-lineage comparisons progressively more diffuse.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Independent methods converging on the known hierarchy supports biological plausibility of the inferred networks.
insights.quote: the two approaches converged on the same biological interpretation despite relying on distinct optimization principles
insights.locator: Assessing the biological value of multi-sample network inference

insights.claim: Aggressive CORNETO pruning of the haematopoietic KPNN cut the network from 9,791 inputs and about 83,000 edges to 66 inputs and 267 edges but dropped accuracy to about 0.58 and macro F1 to about 0.42, shifting prominence from differentiation genes to general metabolic or structural genes.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Interpretability from sparsity can come at the cost of cell-type-specific biology.
insights.quote: aggressive pruning improves interpretability at the expense of cell-type-specific regulatory programmes
insights.locator: Assessing CORNETO across dynamic and stable biological systems

insights.claim: Reintroducing the top 100 informative genes excluded by pruning, which raised active edges from 267 to 11,924, restored accuracy from 0.576 to 0.906 and macro F1 from 0.424 to 0.848 while staying far smaller than the original network.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Selective re-expansion is a cheap post hoc fix that recovers most lost performance while retaining compression.
insights.quote: classification accuracy increased from 0.576 to 0.906, macro F1 increased from 0.424 to 0.848
insights.locator: Selective re-expansion recovers informative biological structure

insights.claim: Bootstrap aggregation on sFBA with the MitoCore model recovered another 8-11 reactions per model in an eight-condition setting (about 8-11% expansion) while keeping over 85% overlap with high-confidence baseline edges, but saturated at 16 conditions.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Bootstrapping improves recall and stability but has diminishing returns as the solution space becomes fully constrained.
insights.quote: bootstrapping recovered another 8–11 reactions per model (~8–11% expansion)
insights.locator: Bootstrap aggregation improves stability and recall

insights.claim: Prior-network completeness strongly determines inference quality: when the Human-GEM graph was downsampled to 20% completeness all iMAT runs returned zero active reactions, 40-60% gave limited signal, and 80-100% enabled higher precision and recall.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Investment in better prior knowledge networks pays off before tuning regularization.
insights.quote: regularization becomes useful only when sufficient prior structure remains available

insights.claim: Increasing the number of jointly modelled conditions from 2 to 16 raised pairwise Jaccard similarity between independent iMAT runs and stabilised network size and sensitivity to lambda.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: More jointly modelled conditions reduce sensitivity to which subset is sampled.
insights.quote: Increasing the number of jointly inferred conditions generally increased the similarity between independently inferred solutions
insights.locator: Increasing the number of jointly modelled conditions improves robustness

insights.claim: Haematopoietic iMAT precision and recall stayed low across lambda values (maximum PPV about 0.20 and TPR about 0.042), with moderate regularization (lambda 0.1-0.25) best and lambda 0.75 or higher over-regularizing.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Absolute iMAT recovery of held-out labels is weak, so moderate coupling is a stability measure rather than an accuracy fix.
insights.quote: reflects excessive sparsity rather than improved recovery
insights.locator: Assessing CORNETO across dynamic and stable biological systems

insights.claim: CORNETO unifies FBA, sparse FBA, iMAT, CARNIVAL and prize-collecting Steiner trees as special cases of one mixed-integer network-flow formulation using structured sparsity penalties, and is open source with modular extensions.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A unified optimisation backbone lowers the cost of combining omics network methods.
insights.quote: provides a unified, knowledge-driven framework that reformulates multi-sample network inference as a mixed-integer constrained optimization problem

insights.claim: The authors expect future adaptive regularization, data-driven sparsification and iterative refinement embedded in agentic or human-in-the-loop workflows to position CORNETO as a backbone for scalable knowledge-driven network inference.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Gestures at agentic automation of network inference tuning without evidence in this paper.
insights.quote: adaptive regularization, data-driven sparsification and iterative refinement strategies embedded in agentic or human-in-the-loop workflows
